prize_parts.citation: for formalising how organised political interests shape trade policy, and for analysing the interplay of trade, innovation and growth

statement.case_for: I keep B001 first after reading the openings. The Grossman-Helpman contribution is an explanatory framework, not a set of isolated findings. It turned a long-standing puzzle, why trade policy departs from efficiency, into a tractable model with testable implications, and it opened a structural empirical literature. The same partnership also supplies the endogenous-growth-in-open-economies strand. Attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist: two people, decades of sustained joint work, and no real dispute about who originated the core models. The work dates from the late 1980s and 1990s and has had three decades of extension, application and critique, so there is no maturity question. I also weigh it on the common criteria, which ask for big questions with societal significance and explanatory power, not on field membership. Public debate about lobbying and protection still draws on this framework.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is empirical. Tests of the protection-for-sale prediction give mixed results, so the work's influence rests more on conceptual and organising power than on decisive confirmation. The award would also be a second trade prize after 2008. Finally, Helpman is credited under both B001 and B020. The committee has to decide which body of his work it is recognising, and a citation covering both lobbying and growth risks being too broad.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B020 (Helpman and Melitz on firm heterogeneity) first. He argues it reorganised trade theory and estimation, has not been recognised since 2008, and is strongly confirmed in micro data. He also flags that Helpman's overlap with B001 could push the committee to combine or split his credit.
responses.response: I agree that firm heterogeneity is a major contribution and that its empirical reach is greater than that of the political-economy models. That is why I list B020 as an alternative. I disagree that the Helpman overlap should favour B020. The two achievements are distinct, and B001 does not depend on B020 for its case. B020's attribution is also less settled by your own account: Redding's role, and the Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum firm-level foundations that are not on the credited list. B001 has no comparable attribution gap. If the committee finds B001's mixed empirical support decisive, I would move toward B020 before I would move to a different field.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B001 last of his eight. He describes it as primarily theory with limited measurement and mixed support for protection-for-sale, and he notes the overlap with B020 on Helpman.
responses.response: I accept the empirical point and treat it as my main reservation. I read it differently, though. A framework can earn a prize through the questions it makes answerable, and Grossman-Helpman did that for the political economy of trade. They gave empiricists a structural equation to estimate, even where estimates vary. Mixed results in applications are the normal outcome for a model with a testable prediction, not evidence the framework failed. I would ask you to separate 'contested magnitudes' from 'no lasting contribution', since B001 appears to me to be the former. I agree that the Helpman overlap with B020 needs an explicit committee choice.

responses.point: Dreber-Almenberg ranks B019 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn) first. She argues the designs are transparent, scrutinised and largely robust, and that Katz is a credible alternative third name but the core empirical credit belongs to the first three.
responses.response: I largely agree and rank B019 second. The China-shock work combines new data, credible identification and an explanatory framework, and I share your trio over Katz. We differ on maturity and attribution. The China-shock papers are from 2013 onward and the long-run persistence of the effects is still debated. The task framework also overlaps with Acemoglu and Restrepo, outside the credited list and tied to a recent laureate. That leaves B019 with a bigger open attribution question than B001. This is a close judgement between two strong candidates, and I would not call B019 weaker on scientific significance.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat Helpman's credit under B001 and B020 as one body of work or two, and which citation framing follows from that.
How much weight the mixed empirical record of the protection-for-sale predictions should carry against the framework's conceptual influence.
Whether the China-shock and task strands in B019 form one coherent achievement, and how the Katz versus Dorn choice and the Acemoglu-Restrepo overlap should be resolved.
My assessments of citations and priority come from recollection of the literature, not independent verification.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My listed frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot ID. My field of labour economics and crime is adjacent to B019 and B014, but no personal or collaborative connection to those candidates is apparent.
